turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. I have twenty minutes.

I got your email about Owen's essay. Then I saw the zero in the portal. It was already entered.

Before we talk about anything else, I need to know one thing. Who in his class knows about this?

Fine. Go ahead.

But I'm keeping track of the clock. And I'm listening for dates, Mr. Hale. Dates, and things I can check.
I have 140 students. I don't have time to be cross-examined by every parent with a law degree.

I'm not here as a lawyer. I'm here as his mother.

And I hear you. A hundred and forty students is a lot.

But a zero is already in the portal. That's fifteen percent of his mark. So I'm asking what it's based on.

One number from a checker isn't something I can verify. What else do you have?
You don't get to talk to me like I'm on the stand.

You're right. That's fair.

I'll ask differently. Walk me through what happened. Start with the day you ran the essay through the checker.

I'll listen. I won't interrupt.

But I do need to know when you ran it, and what else you looked at. That's all I'm asking.
